heroHeadline: Global Reef Study: Under 2% of the Ocean Sits Inside MPAs Showing Real Fish-Biomass Recovery
heroSubtitle: A global synthesis of underwater biodiversity data published September 7, 2026 by University of Tasmania reef ecologist Ella Clausius found that while roughly 10% of the ocean is now officially designated as protected, less than 2% lies within marine protected areas showing measured fish-biomass recovery — and that already-low figure assumes full compliance with fishing rules, which is frequently not the case in practice. The study argues that protection status on paper is a poor substitute for direct underwater monitoring of whether ecosystems are actually recovering. This follows the Government of Jersey's September 1 Marine Spatial Plan expansion tripling trawl-free waters to 21.7% of its territorial sea, and Ocean Conservancy's late-August 2025 International Coastal Cleanup report finding plastic bottles and caps still among the most common items collected from beaches worldwide.
